scenarios.description: Launch-planning midpoint. Every token, route-mix, activation, and behavior input remains an assumption until TestFlight; only the sold-comps query price is measured.

Conservative operating case using higher token volume, retries, provider calls, paid-plan exposure, failures, corrections, and free activation subsidy. Inputs are dated assumptions, not observed percentiles.

Deliberately adverse bound: maximum in-repo model retry envelopes, no sold-comp cache hits, high free activation and correction load, and standard 30% Apple commission. It is a guardrail, not a forecast.

costInventory.note: Free launch capacity; Pro's $25/month enters p90/stress fixed-cost sensitivity, not per-listing COGS.
Local/Free validation first; paid runtime floors enter p90/stress fixed costs. No deployment is authorized.
Marketing hosting is not caused by one native AI-item run; keep it out of listing COGS and review it as a company fixed cost.

costInventory.service: OpenAI vision, pricing, and listing calls
costInventory.note: Token volumes and route shares are dated scenario assumptions; the current public rate card is official.
Inventory only: the modeled showcase path uses OpenAI, while the provider registry keeps Gemini as the development flip.
One few-shot retrieval query is assumed; pgvector's 1536-dimension lock keeps the embedding provider separate from the language-model flip.
Tavily pay-as-you-go is modeled; Exa remains a provider breakpoint/fallback because route mix is unmeasured.
Uses #188's measured $0.091435/query historical evidence, varied by assumed route share and cache hit. Production activation remains default-off.
The measured benchmark produced no usable result and 92.5% block/error; retain only the $49 plan crossover, not a production route assumption.

costInventory.service: Durable queue, storage, egress, logs, and push/email metadata
costInventory.note: Bundled as a dated per-attempt infrastructure range until server metering separates storage, egress, queue, APNs, and email.
One durable free listing is a subsidy. The model allocates an assumed number of free activations to each paid subscriber instead of hiding it in paid-run COGS.
Reruns pricing plus listing generation for the same photo fingerprint and consumes no second credit; correction incidence varies by scenario.

costInventory.service: Failed run, retry, and credit restoration
costInventory.note: The credit restores before durable value, but sunk provider cost remains. Expected failure burden uses f/(1-f) failures per durable success.

costInventory.service: Apple commission, refunds, and indirect tax
costInventory.note: 15% requires Small Business Program eligibility/approval; stress uses 30%. Refund and tax-withheld rates are dated assumptions awaiting RevenueCat/App Store proceeds.
Free through $2,500 monthly tracked revenue; p90/stress apply the 1% marginal rate to avoid hiding the scale breakpoint.
First 1M product analytics events are free; no session replay is required for the decision gate. Event volume is an assumption.

costInventory.service: Clerk, Upstash, Sentry, Resend, and APNs
costInventory.note: Current free tiers cover the planning case; p90/stress fixed-cost bundles include likely paid-plan floors. APNs has no separate modeled marginal fee.

sources.title: Issue #188 sold-comps live benchmark
sources.note: 40-query historical run: $3.6574 spend, $0.091435/query, 95% retrieval coverage, 0 retries; production activation rejected in the original report.

sources.title: Issue #188 provider-neutral matcher replay
sources.note: 16/40 queries reached two anchors, 91.53% anchor precision, and 40.91% valid-comparable recall; saved capture only.

sources.title: Issue #195 runtime and hosting proof
sources.note: Air-gapped orchestration lower bound plus an explicitly assumed provider-inclusive 120-second/10-active-CPU-second/512-MiB envelope.

sources.title: Issue #168 AI-item credit ledger
sources.note: Reserve, settle once on durable value, restore once before value, monthly StoreKit period, and one guided correction semantics.

sources.title: ADR-0008 native entitlements and credits
sources.note: Free activation, included correction, monthly allowance, annual monthly reset, and no-rollover/unlimited product boundary.

sources.title: Current pipeline implementation
sources.note: Current extraction, optional garment measurement, pricing, listing, and bounded retry seams used to define cost stages.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-5.5 API pricing
sources.note: $5/M input, $0.50/M cached input, and $30/M output; token volumes are not yet measured.

sources.title: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small pricing
sources.note: $0.02/M input tokens.

sources.title: Google Gemini API pricing
sources.note: Gemini 2.5 Flash paid tier: $0.30/M text-image-video input and $2.50/M output; development free tier exists.

sources.title: Tavily API credits
sources.note: 1,000 free monthly credits and $0.008/credit pay-as-you-go; basic search is one credit.

sources.title: Exa API pricing
sources.note: 20,000 free requests/month; Search $7/1,000 and Contents $1/1,000 pages after the free tier.

sources.title: Caffein eBay sold listings actor
sources.note: Current public card says from $2.50/1,000 results. The model intentionally uses #188's measured historical run cost instead of retrofitting it.

sources.title: ScrapingBee pricing
sources.note: $49/month for 250,000 credits on the lowest public plan.

sources.title: Apple Developer Program
sources.note: $99/year membership; APNs and TestFlight are included capabilities, with no separate APNs marginal fee modeled.

sources.title: App Store Small Business Program
sources.note: 15% commission for eligible enrolled developers up to the program threshold; enrollment is not assumed approved.

sources.title: Apple Developer Program License Agreement
sources.note: Apple deducts commission and applicable taxes and accounts for refunds; exact proceeds require live App Store/RevenueCat evidence.

sources.title: RevenueCat pricing
sources.note: Free through $2,500 in monthly tracked revenue, then 1% of tracked revenue.

sources.title: PostHog pricing
sources.note: First 1M product analytics events/month free; mobile replay has a separate 2,500 free recording allowance and is excluded from the minimum gate.

sources.title: Supabase pricing
sources.note: Free plan limits and Pro from $25/month define step-variable breakpoints; no production plan mutation is authorized.

sources.title: Vercel pricing
sources.note: Pro is $20/month with included usage; marketing hosting is separated from native API/worker economics.

sources.title: Render pricing
sources.note: Free and Starter compute prices define a deferred runtime breakpoint; no deployment is authorized.

sources.title: Railway pricing
sources.note: Free, $5 Hobby, and $20 Pro plan floors are inventoried behind ADR-0009's owner-controlled trigger.

sources.title: Clerk pricing
sources.note: Hobby includes 50,000 MRU; Pro begins at $25 monthly or $20/month billed annually.

sources.title: Upstash Redis pricing
sources.note: Free includes 500,000 commands; pay-as-you-go is $0.20/100,000 commands before storage/bandwidth overages.

sources.title: Sentry pricing
sources.note: Developer is free; Team starts at $26/month billed annually. Paid-plan exposure is fixed, not per listing.

sources.title: Resend pricing
sources.note: Free includes 3,000 emails/month; Pro is $20 for 50,000. Email is not required per successful listing.

excludedCosts.reason: Legacy web billing is not the native StoreKit/RevenueCat launch path.

excludedCosts.service: eBay seller fees, shipping, and taxes
excludedCosts.reason: These affect the seller's transaction economics, not SnapList subscription COGS.
They occur after listing creation and are not part of one complete AI-item credit.
Offline product-quality evaluation is not a per-customer listing path.
Issue #189 authorizes analysis only; no account, plan, credential, deployment, or routing mutation.
